items.title: cGAN factorial canary
items.rollback_or_fallback: Use configs/vnncomp25/cgan_2023.yaml and omit every cgan_recipe factorial arm.
items.rationale: UNCHANGED disposition, CORRECTED reason. The July verdict rested partly on arms that cannot measure anything. 2 of the 13 cgan_recipe arms carry `general.device: wgpu`, and `preset::contract::validate_preset` (crates/ny-cli/src/preset/contract.rs:276) classifies a wgpu request as Unhonoured/PerformanceOnly - 'the requested backend is overridden with the sound CPU verifier' while WGPU proof authority is quarantined. `device_wgpu` changes ONLY that key, so it is byte-identical to `baseline` BY CONSTRUCTION and is INERT; `supported_upstream_bundle` silently measures 9 of its 10 fields. scripts/run_abcrown_transfer_factorials.py does not surface unhonoured-field warnings, so an inert arm is indistinguishable from a real one in its output. Both arms are now annotated in configs/experiments/abcrown_transfer_factorials.yaml. No solved-count win is claimed or refuted here; the point is that two arms never tested what their names say. [lane3-requalify-20260809 @ HEAD efb15df8, GB10 CUDA (CudaGemmEngine on NVIDIA GB10), official budgets]

items.title: CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet preset parity
items.rollback_or_fallback: Run the unchanged category presets with no cifar100_recipe or tinyimagenet_recipe factorial override.
items.rationale: MEASURED NULL AND NOT EXERCISED (re-measured 2026-08-09 on GB10 CUDA at the official 100 s budget; see docs/TINYIMAGENET_PARITY_A2_NOT_EXERCISED_2026-08-09.md). Arming the full cross-category parity bundle on tinyimagenet_2024 (batch_size 128->256, candidates 10->7, min_batch_size_ratio, max_split_depth, kfsb_multi, alpha_crown.lr_alpha 0.2->0.25, beta_crown.lr_beta 0.15->0.2, beta_crown.iterations 15->10, the clip block, root_crown_interm_dense_head) is NET +0/-0 over 44 paired runs on 22 rows: 0 of 10 sampled GT-unsat rows ny misses converted, and the 12 rows ny banks came back with identical per-class tallies. The arms were confirmed LIVE from the run's effective_config receipt, so this is a not-exercised result rather than a vacuous one: the internal verifier reports domains_explored=0 in ALL 44 runs, and every key except root_crown_interm_dense_head is consumed inside the BaB loop. The category's unsat verdicts come from the concurrent margin-row lane, whose entry point run_margin_row_lane takes no BetaCrownConfig, so no bab.* key can reach it by signature; the lane's published root_bound is identical between arms on every row where both published (5/5). One banked wall-hugger (prop_idx_5478) closes 4/4 under the shipped preset and 2/4 under parity, so the bundle never paid and marginally costs. PROVENANCE NOTE: this entry's default_changed=false is accurate for both halves, but must not be read as 'cifar100 does not carry these values' - git log -S dates five of them (batch_size 256, candidates 7, lr_alpha 0.25, lr_beta 0.2, iterations 10) to 3c6c271b 'Initial ny rebrand' (2026-05-24) and the other two to cifar100-scoped waves 35e72d2e (2026-07-21) and 355d24b3 (2026-07-23). None came from this transfer campaign.

items.title: VGG graph and branching recipe
items.rollback_or_fallback: Leave model.vgg_abcrown_treatment unset and use configs/vnncomp25/vggnet16_2022.yaml.
items.rationale: The scoped MaxPool rewrite and treatment policy have equivalence and gate-off coverage, but no official-budget conversion of a previously open VGG property has been sealed.

items.title: Skip the final unusable alpha gradient pass
items.rollback_or_fallback: Unset NY_ALPHA_FINAL_BOUND_ONLY to execute the legacy final gradient, probe, refresh, and update path.
items.rationale: UNCHANGED disposition, and the ceiling is far LOWER than 'a missing speedup result' implies. REACHABILITY (read at 6 production sites): on DAG/graph models the three collection entry points (crates/ny-propagate/src/network/graph_alpha/propagate_dag/collect.rs:38/58/78) pass `DagAlphaLoopResultUse::BoundsAndState`, and `terminal_bound_only()` is `gate_enabled && matches!(self, BoundsOnly)` (propagate_dag/mod.rs:143), so B1 FAILS CLOSED on every DAG root-alpha collection - the expensive alpha phase that warm-starts BaB. The collection core says so itself: 'Collection always marks the returned state as observable.' B1 is live only via propagate_dag/mod.rs:637 (BoundsOnly bound query) and alpha_crown_loop.rs:782 (sequential `alpha_crown_optimize`). CEILING where live: it removes exactly 1 of `iterations` alpha iterations (<=5% of the alpha phase at `iterations: 20`), WALL ONLY - it cannot move a bound, so it cannot convert a bound-quality row. MEASURED at the official 116s budget on acasxu_2023 1_1/prop_1, 3 arms x 3 repeats: unsat 9/9, 29 domains explored / 88 verified in EVERY arm, root bound [-342.0013, 1294.4406] identical in every arm - verdict- and bound-neutral as designed. At -vv (DEBUG) the 'NY_ALPHA_FINAL_BOUND_ONLY terminal pass' marker fired 0 times in 32,986 DEBUG lines: on this route B1 is NOT EXERCISED, which is not the same as neutral. [lane3-requalify-20260809 @ HEAD efb15df8, GB10 CUDA (CudaGemmEngine on NVIDIA GB10), official budgets]

items.title: CUDA-wide refold guard and fallback
items.rollback_or_fallback: Any refold mismatch or oracle error falls back to the serial loop; NY_CUDA_WIDE=0 disables the parent CUDA-wide route.
items.rationale: The serial refold oracle and fail-closed rejection handling are promoted within the already default-dark CUDA-wide parent route; this is not a global CUDA-wide promotion.

items.title: Reuse the existing root-alpha fold
items.rollback_or_fallback: Leave NY_ROOT_ALPHA_GPU unset; the existing warmup gradient path performs its reference extraction and fold.
items.rationale: Cache and skeleton reuse machinery exists, but the root-alpha reuse treatment remains scoped and lacks the required median root or alpha wall result.

items.title: Sparse unstable intermediate-bound queue storage
items.rollback_or_fallback: Keep dense DomainList layer-bound storage; the standalone SparseLayerBounds representation remains non-authoritative.
items.rationale: The sparse representation has local differential coverage but was not promoted into a queue family and has no qualifying queue-memory and throughput result; root sparse CROWN is a different mechanism.

items.title: Packed per-domain alpha state
items.rollback_or_fallback: Use the nested-map GraphDomainAlphaState representation and its existing DomainList round-trip path.
items.rationale: UNCHANGED disposition, but the ledger's '5% queue-throughput result' framing is misleading: the throughput gate was never measurable on the categories it was aimed at, because C2 is OFF-ROUTE there. The gate is read at EXACTLY ONE production site - crates/ny-propagate/src/batched_domain/domain_list/storage.rs:705, inside `DomainList::add`. The only production `DomainList` constructors are gpu_bab/init.rs:310 and gpu_bab/input_split.rs:585, both reached only through `verify_graph_gpu_domain_list`, which runs only when `gpu_bab` is true. `should_auto_promote_gpu_bab` (crates/ny-cli/src/commands/beta_crown/mod.rs:2234) grants that only for graph models whose branching heuristic is BoundImpact or InputSplit and which are not generic multi-clause disjunctions (its own comment names cGAN and ml4acopf as deliberately excluded). cifar100_2024 and tinyimagenet_2024 set NO `bab.branching.method` at all, and at RUNTIME the auto-selector logs 'Auto-branching selected Kfsb: high-dimensional input or large unstable-ReLU frontier (ReLU/kFSB splitting)' with input_elements=3072 (cifar100) and 9408 (tinyimagenet). Kfsb is in neither admitted class, so gpu_bab is never promoted. Note this is driven by the benchmark's own shape, not by a preset omission: no preset edit reaches C2 without changing the branching strategy wholesale. MEASURED: 'DomainList BaB:' is an INFO-level marker emitted on EVERY path of that function including all early returns, and it appears 0 times in every run of acasxu_2023, cifar100_2024 and tinyimagenet_2024 at official budgets. So on cgan, relusplitter, cifar100, tinyimagenet AND acasxu, C2 is NOT EXERCISED - report it as off-route, never as throughput-neutral. The 51.5% per-domain memory reduction is real but unrealised: to qualify C2 at all it must be measured on a category that actually builds a DomainList (input-split, non-disjunctive: nn4sys, linearizenn_2024, dist_shift_2023, cersyve, lsnc_relu). [lane3-requalify-20260809 @ HEAD efb15df8, GB10 CUDA (CudaGemmEngine on NVIDIA GB10), official budgets]

items.title: Reduce DomainList copies
items.rollback_or_fallback: Use the owned-copy TensorStorage and PooledArray path for unsupported, alias-uncertain, or small-queue cases.
items.rationale: NOT ARMABLE - it needs implementing, not arming, and the previous rationale reads as though a gate existed and failed its promotion bar. There is NO env var and NO preset key anywhere in the tree for this item: all three of its own evidence paths (crates/ny-tensor/src/pooled_array.rs, crates/ny-tensor/src/tensor_storage/mod.rs, crates/ny-propagate/src/batched_domain/picked_conversion.rs) contain zero `env::var` reads, and no `bab.*` preset field maps to it. Its shipped parts (PooledArray no-restack conversion, cached lA retention) are already default-on. Any future 'C3 measured X' claim is unsupportable until a gate exists. [lane3-requalify-20260809 @ HEAD efb15df8, GB10 CUDA (CudaGemmEngine on NVIDIA GB10), official budgets]

items.title: In-iteration physical pruning
items.rollback_or_fallback: Retain the dense optimization batch and logical verified-lane masking without physical gather and scatter.
items.rationale: No complete physical compaction increment with full-index restoration and randomized AND/OR mapping oracles reached the campaign, so the proposed transfer is killed rather than inferred from logical masking.

items.title: Memory-aware batching across BaB routes
items.rollback_or_fallback: Leave NY_ADAPTIVE_MICROBATCH_CONTROLLER unset; existing auto_enlarge_batch_size presets retain their legacy one-way growth and fallback behavior.
items.rationale: The independently gated controller now covers graph ReLU-split and DomainList input-split with ordered reason-coded backoff, but its device budget is not a live CUDA allocator query and it lacks a qualifying hardware throughput result.

items.title: Precomputed decisions with adaptive lA retention
items.rollback_or_fallback: Retain cached lA and recompute or validate branch decisions through the existing post-dequeue path.
items.rationale: Branch decisions can already be formed from batched child tensors and cached lA survives queue operations, but no adaptive drop-versus-retain policy meets the byte, mapping, or throughput gates.

items.title: Persistent CUDA transaction
items.rollback_or_fallback: Leave NY_CUDA_DGEMM_TRIPLET unset and use the serial sound CUDA GEMM route.
items.rationale: The triplet transaction is sound and measured behind an exact gate, but 3-to-1 synchronization is below the 80 percent target and upload, 100-wave high-water, two-row NVIDIA, and end-to-end gains are absent.

items.title: Expanded shared-batch eligibility
items.rollback_or_fallback: Use the reason-coded serial or per-domain fallback for every excluded caller mode.
items.rationale: No excluded surface met all eligibility, mapping, throughput, and solved-count gates; the pure-chain candidate was refuted and the other unsupported surfaces remain fail-closed.

subarms.rollback_or_fallback: Leave NY_BAB_CHAIN_WIDE unset and use the dense serial reference route.
subarms.rationale: The differential oracle found the wide replacement looser and measured work included a solved-row timeout regression.

subarms.rollback_or_fallback: Keep unsupported_caller_mode routing to the sequential conjunctive evaluator.
subarms.rationale: The batch planner deliberately excludes conjunctive mode, yielding zero target-lane shared-batch eligibility.

subarms.rollback_or_fallback: Keep optimize_disjuncts_separately false or fall back to the serial per-disjunct evaluator on any batched error.
subarms.rationale: The opt-in packed pseudo-domain path has functional coverage but lacks mapping-trajectory, fallback-rate, throughput, and solved-count promotion evidence.

subarms.rollback_or_fallback: Route any nonempty active cut pool through the existing per-domain fallback.
subarms.rationale: Shared batching requires cuts inactive; overall cuts parity tests do not demonstrate an active-cut shared-batch lane.

items.title: Fixed-domain alpha-beta-CROWN diagnostic oracle
items.rollback_or_fallback: The diagnostic is read-only; omit capture or record commands and verifier execution is unchanged.
items.rationale: The immutable corpus, provenance-bound capture, canonical row schema, and comparison-ready phase and bound metrics are promoted as diagnostic infrastructure, not as a verifier treatment.

items.title: Targeted reverse-mode bound gradients
items.rollback_or_fallback: Disable the affected wide route or use its serial and SPSA fallbacks; unsupported operators continue to use SPSA.
items.rationale: Only existing fused wide beta-gradient capture is promoted; analytic SPSA replacements, independent upper differentiation, conditional derivative edges, and wide alpha do not receive promotion by association.

subarms.rollback_or_fallback: Set NY_RESNET_BETA_GPU=0, NY_BAB_RESNET_BATCHED=0, or NY_BAB_RESNET_WIDE_BETA=0 to select the reference route.
subarms.rationale: One wide backward returns sound bounds and per-ReLU beta gathers, with serial or CPU fallback and historical fixed-wall throughput gains.

subarms.rollback_or_fallback: Preserve SPSA for MulBinary, monotone S-shaped functions, Sqrt, Reciprocal, unsupported operators, and nonfinite analytic refusal.
subarms.rationale: The named operator supplements remain SPSA and no analytic implementation completed the finite-difference, trajectory, lower-upper, soundness, and end-to-end gates.

subarms.rollback_or_fallback: Retain the documented AnalyticChain lower-gradient reuse for the upper path.
subarms.rationale: AnalyticChain still does not separate upper and lower differentiation and has no candidate oracle or performance result.

subarms.rollback_or_fallback: Keep the existing derivative mapping; reopen only after an F1 first-divergence artifact identifies a concrete defect.
subarms.rationale: This conditional target has no identified missing or mis-mapped edge, while existing residual fanout already has finite-difference coverage.

subarms.rollback_or_fallback: Leave NY_BAB_RESNET_WIDE_ALPHA unset; NY_WIDE_ALPHA_CPU remains the differential reference when the experiment is enabled.
subarms.rationale: Wide alpha has finite-difference and device-oracle evidence, but the local rule regressed and the true joint adjoint lacks fixed-budget solved-count and bound-quality promotion evidence.

items.title: Later search-policy experiments
items.rollback_or_fallback: Use existing single-mode branching, input-space attack, and zero input-split alpha refinement outside explicitly scoped presets.
items.rationale: Selective input-split alpha remains a scoped experiment; the other three search ideas have no candidate with solved-count evidence and are recorded kills for this campaign.

subarms.rollback_or_fallback: Keep the existing default-off BICCOS-lite cut controls and ordinary BaB search.
subarms.rationale: The repository contains proactive BICCOS-lite but no full multi-tree shallow-search state, gate, oracle, or solved-count result.

subarms.rollback_or_fallback: Select one existing BranchingHeuristic, including InputSplit or an activation heuristic.
subarms.rationale: The branching enum exposes separate input and activation choices but no hybrid policy or solved-count candidate.

subarms.rollback_or_fallback: Use the existing concrete input-space post-BaB DLR or APGD attack, or disable it with NY_POSTBAB_ATTACK=0.
subarms.rationale: Current post-BaB attacks consume input-space centers and frontier boxes; no activation-space attack implementation or solved-count result exists.

subarms.rollback_or_fallback: Keep input_split_alpha_iteration at zero and input_split_edge_alpha false outside explicitly selected presets.
subarms.rationale: Warm and edge-alpha refinement have soundness and gate-default tests, but benchmark evidence is mixed and does not support a global solved-count promotion.
